name: Emily Dickinson
hook: The Belle of Amherst wrote the short, strange poems Jeopardy quotes more than almost any other verse.

facts.label: Amherst, Massachusetts
facts.statement: She lived almost her whole life in Amherst, Massachusetts, and died there in 1886.

facts.label: "Because I could not stop for Death"
facts.statement: "Because I could not stop for Death" has Death kindly stopping for her and a carriage holding just the two of them.

facts.label: hope
facts.statement: She calls hope "the thing with feathers that perches in the soul."

facts.label: "I heard a Fly buzz"
facts.statement: She wrote "I heard a Fly buzz — when I died."

facts.label: "I'm Nobody!"
facts.statement: She wrote "I'm Nobody! Who are you? Are you — Nobody — too?"

facts.label: "There is no Frigate like a Book"
facts.statement: She wrote "There is no Frigate like a Book / To take us Lands away."

facts.label: the Civil War
facts.statement: She wrote hundreds of poems during the Civil War.
